stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Google stop short of AI safety guarantee
stories.simple_summary: Big AI companies like OpenAI and Google won't promise that their AI systems are completely safe — they're saying they'll try but can't guarantee it.
stories.why_it_matters: This honestly doesn't affect your daily life much right now. It's mainly about what rules the government should make.

stories.title: Trump AI Task Force Faces Pressure to Move Beyond Voluntary Guardrails
stories.simple_summary: The government's new AI task force is being pushed to set stronger rules instead of just asking companies to follow guidelines on their own.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a political story about regulation — it won't directly change how you use AI today.

stories.title: In Race With U.S., China Struggles to Recruit Foreign A.I. Researchers
stories.simple_summary: China is having trouble hiring foreign AI researchers, putting them behind the U.S. in the competition to build better AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters mainly to investors and people following international competition — nothing affecting your local business.

stories.title: France's Mistral launches AI model it says outperforms some Chinese rivals
stories.simple_summary: A French company called Mistral created a new AI system that they say works as well as or better than some AI systems made by Chinese companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly interesting to tech investors and engineers — it doesn't affect what AI tools you have access to yet.

stories.title: Pinterest’s AI now turns beauty Pins into action plans
stories.simple_summary: Pinterest's AI can now look at pictures of hairstyles or nails and tell you what a salon would call the look, what it might cost, how long it takes, and how to maintain it.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Pinterest and like beauty ideas, this could help you actually book salon appointments instead of just saving pictures.

stories.title: Get all your questions answered at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: The full breakout session agenda revealed
stories.simple_summary: TechCrunch is advertising their annual tech conference happening in October 2026 in San Francisco and offering discounted registration.
stories.why_it_matters: This is just an advertisement — only relevant if you're interested in attending a tech conference.

stories.title: The Only 2 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks I'd Buy With $1,000 Today and Never Sell
stories.simple_summary: Someone is recommending two specific AI company stocks they think people should buy and hold for a long time.
stories.why_it_matters: This is investment advice from one person's opinion — talk to a real financial advisor before buying any stocks based on headlines.

stories.title: Amazon Alexa Plus keeps creepily singing ‘lalala’ for minutes on end
stories.simple_summary: Some people with Amazon Alexa speakers are experiencing a bug where the device gets stuck saying or singing "lalala" over and over for several minutes.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own an Echo speaker, this might be a bug you encounter, but Amazon will likely fix it soon — it's not a permanent problem.

stories.title: Introducing GLM 5.3 on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
stories.simple_summary: Amazon announced a new AI model called GLM 5.3 that businesses can use through Amazon's cloud service.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a tech product announcement aimed at companies and engineers — nothing you need to know about unless you run a tech business.

stories.title: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late
stories.simple_summary: Google is working on a feature where you can tell an AI to make phone calls for you, like calling your mom to say you'll be late.
stories.why_it_matters: This could save you time on routine calls, but it's still in testing — not available to everyone yet.

stories.title: AI expert Gary Marcus warns 'reckless' technology could lead to deaths as he calls for more regulation
stories.simple_summary: An AI expert named Gary Marcus is warning that careless development of AI could eventually cause deaths and is calling for stricter government rules.
stories.why_it_matters: This is one expert's opinion about long-term safety — it's part of an ongoing debate but doesn't change anything you're doing today.

stories.title: OpenAI will start watermarking ChatGPT’s text in the EU
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI will add invisible watermarks to text written by ChatGPT in Europe to follow new EU rules that track AI-generated content.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use ChatGPT in Europe, your outputs will be marked as AI-made, which could matter if you're submitting work to a school or employer.
